why: All three checks confirm the finding. (1) DOC: curl of https://code.claude.com/docs/en/auto-mode-config.md yields the sentence VERBATIM at line 182 -- "To keep the built-in rules while adding your own, include the literal string `"$defaults"` in the array." The rest of that line strengthens rather than reverses it: "The default rules are spliced in at that position, so your custom rules can go before or after them, and you continue to inherit updates as the built-in list changes across releases." Line 103 says the same for `environment`, and the Danger callout at :212 pins the other half: "Setting any of `environment`, `allow`, `soft_deny`, or `hard_deny` without `"$defaults"` replaces the entire default list for that section," naming force push, curl|bash, production deploys and the data-exfiltration rule as what is lost. `auto-mode-config` is row 62 of scripts/claude-doc-pages.tsv, so it is a Claude contract page. (2) CITES: managed-policy.ts:1061-1067 is `resolveAutoModeList`, which flatMaps AUTO_MODE_DEFAULTS_SENTINEL ('$defaults', :478) to `[...defaults]`; `resolveAutoMode` (:1082) takes `defaults: Partial<ResolvedAutoModePolicyV1> = {}` and composes `resolveAutoModeList(scopes.managed?.[key], defaults[key] ?? [])` plus `resolveAutoModeList(scopes.user?.[key], [])` (:1092-1093). SessionManager.ts:4109 is `resolveAutoMode({ managed: this.managedPiPolicy.autoMode })` -- no second argument. guardian.ts:342-348 builds the judge's org-policy section from exactly the four lists. (3) CONSEQUENCE, verified separately from the identifier: an exhaustive `grep -ran 'resolveAutoMode('` (with -a, so NUL-byte files are not skipped) over the repo excluding node_modules/dist finds ONE production caller -- SessionManager.ts:4109 -- and no other; `resolveAutoModeList` has no production caller outside the module; no DEFAULT_AUTO_MODE/AUTO_MODE_DEFAULTS list constant exists anywhere. A live probe importing the real module printed: resolveAutoModeList(['a','$defaults','b'], ['D1']) -> ['a','D1','b'] (the mechanism works when fed defaults), but the production shape resolveAutoMode({managed:{allow:['$defaults','x'], soft_deny:['$defaults']}}) -> {environment:[],hard_deny:[],soft_deny:[],allow:['x']} and resolveAutoMode({managed:{allow:['x']}}) -> the identical object. So the sentinel is silently swallowed, with and without it producing byte-identical judge input. The shipped test managed-policy.test.ts:1025 already pins that (`.allow` equals `['x']`). One layer down: our built-in rules are unconditional prose in GUARDIAN_POLICY_PROMPT (guardian.ts:121-238 -- sections 'Data Exfiltration', 'Credential Probing', 'Persistent Security Weakening', 'Destructive Actions'), installed as `systemPrompt` at guardian-judge-core.ts:110 and never touched by the org-policy path, which only APPENDS a '## Organization policy' section (guardian.ts:382-383). So omitting `$defaults` discards nothing either. Sibling-subsystem check: `managedAutoMode` is Pi-only (SessionManager.ts:4108 gates on provider==='pi'); the Claude backend has no autoMode passthrough, so there is no second implementation that could be honouring the contract elsewhere. NOT a recorded owner decision: inert-worklist section 3 item 3 is `autoMode.classifyAllShell` -- a different key, and closed by audit row D1 on 2026-07-30 (a306b17f). NOT a rebrand or dropped-subscription product difference. The nearest recorded deviation, deviation-register:363, covers only auto-mode-config.md:246's missing `claude auto-mode defaults/config/reset` CLI surface; it never states that the splice sentinel resolves to nothing, so it corroborates the root cause rather than refuting the finding.
correctedState: CONFIRMED, with the direction of harm narrowed. The `$defaults` sentinel is parsed (AUTO_MODE_DEFAULTS_SENTINEL, managed-policy.ts:478) and the splice mechanism is correct and tested, but no built-in rule lists exist in this fork to splice: the sole production caller, SessionManager.ts:4109, calls resolveAutoMode with no defaults argument, and the user scope is hardcoded to [] at managed-policy.ts:1093, so a managed `['$defaults', 'x']` and a managed `['x']` produce byte-identical judge input (verified by live probe). Nessy's built-in rules live as unconditional prose in GUARDIAN_POLICY_PROMPT (guardian.ts:121) rather than as the four addressable environment/hard_deny/soft_deny/allow lists the page describes, and that prompt is installed as the judge's system prompt at guardian-judge-core.ts:110 regardless of any autoMode block. Consequence in both directions: including the sentinel adds nothing (it is silently dropped, with no diagnostic to the admin, the same honesty shape as the closed D1 classifyAllShell row), and omitting it discards nothing -- the documented Danger case is unreachable, so an admin who omits `$defaults` intending to take full ownership of soft_deny still gets the built-in taxonomy applied. The failure is therefore fail-safe on enforcement and misleading on configuration, not a hole that drops built-in protections.
